extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, IP practitioners, corporate counsel, USPTO staff, and policy makers
extracted.subtask_short: AIA vs pre-AIA patent law comparison
extracted.subtask_description: A comparative chart summarizing selected differences between pre-America Invents Act (pre-AIA) U.S. patent law and the AIA, listing statutory changes, procedural provisions, effective dates, and mandated studies. Useful for practitioners and policy makers tracking how substantive and procedural patent standards changed under the AIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Inventor to File / First to Invent
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparison of pre-AIA first-to-invent rules (§102(g) interference proceedings to determine earlier inventor) with AIA's first-inventor-to-file regime. AIA replaces first-to-invent concepts with a system where effective filing date governs rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under AIA §102(a)(2) precludes a patent if the claimed invention was described in a patent or patent application naming another inventor and "effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention." Effective: March 16, 2013; applies to claims with effective filing date on or after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Definitions (§102 / §103 changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-AIA §§102/103 defined prior art by knowledge/use in U.S., printed publications, public use/on sale (and 12-month grace). AIA revises §102 to preclude patents for inventions patented, described in a printed publication, or "in public use, on sale or otherwise available to the public" anywhere before the inventor's effective filing date; §103's timing language likewise shifts to before the effective filing of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AIA §102(a)(1) and §102(a)(2) incorporate patents/published applications as prior art with effective filing date doctrines (foreign filing dates can be prior art); In re Hilmer overruled. "On sale" interpreted as publicly on sale. Applicable to claims with effective filing dates on/after March 16, 2013.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace Period (AIA §102(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA replaces the pre-AIA 12-month grace language with narrower exceptions: a disclosure is not prior art if made by the inventor (or someone who obtained the subject matter from the inventor) within one year before the effective filing date, or if the subject matter was previously publicly disclosed by the inventor (or someone who obtained it from the inventor) before the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective March 16, 2013. Applies to patent applications and patents containing claims with effective filing dates on/after March 16, 2013. The chart reproduces statutory phrasing: §102(b)(1) conditions (A) and (B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivation Proceedings (§135 & §291)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA adds derivation proceedings allowing an applicant to petition the USPTO alleging that an earlier application named an inventor who derived the invention from the petitioner. Provides procedures and timing for such petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §135 petitions must be filed within one year after publication of a claim that is the same or substantially the same as the earlier application's claim; USPTO may correct inventorship under §135. §291 gives civil action relief within one year after issuance of the first patent if the later patent derived the invention. Effective March 16, 2013 for claims with effective filing dates on/after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's Oath / Assignee Filing (§115, §118)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-AIA required an oath including belief of original and first inventor and inventor deemed to be the applicant; assignee filing permitted under certain conditions. AIA revises timing and permits assignee filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AIA requires name and an oath or declaration of the inventor to be filed prior to notice of allowance; assignee may file application and is deemed the applicant. Corrections regarding inventorship may be made and failure to comply does not render patent invalid if remedied. Effective for applications filed on or after September 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior User Rights (§273 expansion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-AIA §273(b) allowed prior user defense for certain business method inventions reduced to practice and commercially used in the U.S. AIA expands prior user rights to all subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defense applies to internal commercial uses or arm's length sales of a useful end result made one year before the effective filing date or public disclosure. Defense unavailable where the patented invention was owned/obligated to an institution of higher education/tech transfer org. Effective for any patent issued on or after September 16, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Grant Review (PGR) (§321-329)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA creates PGR procedures permitting third parties to petition to cancel one or more patent claims within nine months of issue/reissue on broad grounds of unpatentability (except best mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §324 allows institution where it is more likely than not at least one challenged claim is unpatentable OR the petition raises a novel/unsettled legal question. Petitioner may assert any invalidity grounds (except best mode) and rely on patents, printed publications, affidavits/declarations. Patent owner may file one motion to amend. Estoppel attaches after final decision; PGR is unavailable if petitioner first filed a civil action. Final decision within one year (six-month extension for good cause). Effective on/after Sept 16, 2012 for patents issued/reissued less than nine months (limited to first-inventor-to-file).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter Partes Review (IPR) (§311-318)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA replaces inter partes reexamination with IPR before PTAB: third parties may petition to institute IPR nine months or more after issue/reissue or after PGR concludes, but generally not later than one year after being sued for infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §314 grants institution if reasonable likelihood petitioner would prevail with respect to at least one challenged claim. Petitioner may assert only §§102 and 103 grounds and rely on patents/printed publications/affidavits/declarations. §316 allows one motion to amend; §316 limits discovery; §315 addresses relationship to other proceedings (estoppel, stays). Settlement permitted under §317 without estoppel. Final decision within one year (six-month extension). Effective September 16, 2012 for any patent issued before, on, or after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of Prior Art in Applications by Third Parties (§122 amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA allows third parties to submit patents, published patent applications or other printed publications for inclusion in the record of a patent application within specified time windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions permitted before notice of allowance, within six months after publication date, or by the date of first rejection, whichever is earlier. Effective September 16, 2012 for any application filed before, on, or after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue for USPTO (change to EDVA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory venue listing for USPTO changed from the United States District Court for the District of Columbia to the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment effective September 16, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Fees / USPTO Fee-Setting Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA grants the USPTO Director authority to set and adjust patent and trademark fees to recover estimated processing costs; retains small entity discounts and creates micro-entity category with larger reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director must publish proposed fee changes in the Federal Register and allow 45 days for public comment; Patent Public Advisory Committee and Congress may comment. Fee reductions: 50% for small entities; 75% for micro entities (criteria enumerated). 15% automatic surcharge added to pre-AIA fees effective September 26, 2011. Fee setting authority sunsets September 16, 2018. Effective Sept 16, 2011 for authority; surcharge effective Sept 26, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Filing Incentive (non-electronic filing surcharge)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA imposes a fee for patent applications not filed electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A $400 fee charged for each patent application not filed electronically. Effective 60 days from Sept 16, 2011 (Nov 15, 2011).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Examination (§257)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA adds supplemental examination allowing patent owners to request reconsideration of information believed relevant to the patent to address issues such as inequitable conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO orders supplemental examination if a substantial new question of patentability is raised by information in the request; must be conducted within three months following ex parte reexamination procedures. A patent cannot be held unenforceable if the information was considered/reconsidered/corrected in supplemental examination. Director must refer potential material fraud to the Attorney General. Supplemental examination must conclude before an allegation is pled in civil action. Effective Sept 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax Strategy Patents (non-patentable subject matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA deems inventions directed to reducing, avoiding, or deferring tax liability to be within the prior art and thus not patentable, with limited exceptions for severable parts used solely for preparing/filing tax returns or financial management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to applications pending on or filed on or after Sept 16, 2011 and patents issued on/after that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Mode Requirement (§112 / §282 change)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA retains the statutory best mode disclosure requirement but removes failure to disclose best mode as a basis for invalidity or unenforceability under §282.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive best mode disclosure still required by §112, but §282 states failure to disclose best mode shall not be a basis for invalidity or unenforceability. Effective Sept 16, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual Marking & False Patent Marking (§287 amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA amends marking rules to allow patentees to use an Internet address that associates the patented article with the patent number instead of physical marking, and changes false marking enforcement standing and remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the U.S. may sue for penalty for false marking on earlier pre-AIA text; AIA permits any person to sue with half the penalty to the suing person and half to U.S.; a person who has suffered competitive injury may sue for damages. Marking with an expired patent number is not a violation. Amendments apply to all cases pending or commenced on/after Sept 16, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice of Counsel (§298)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA adds §298 providing that failure to obtain advice of counsel may not be used to prove willful infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective for patents issued on or after Sept 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of Business-Method Patents (transitional PGR)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA creates a transitional post-grant review for certain business-method patents (methods for performing data processing and operations used in administration of financial products/services), limited by technological invention exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only a party sued or charged with infringement may request review. Final PTAB decision precludes raising same grounds in civil action or before the ITC. If patent under review is at issue in infringement action, parties may seek a stay; court decision immediately appealable to Federal Circuit. Effective Sept 16, 2012; sunsets Sept 16, 2020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder of Parties (§299)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA restricts joinder of defendants in patent civil actions: defendants can be joined only if relief is asserted jointly/severally or arises from same transaction/occurrence relating to the making/using/importing of the same accused product or process and if common questions of fact exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties ineligible for joinder when there are mere allegations they may have infringed. Effective Sept 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO Funding / Ending Fee Diversion (Reserve Fund / §42 changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA amends §42 to create a USPTO Reserve Fund in the U.S. Treasury to hold fee collections in excess of annual appropriation but does not make fees available without an appropriation (fee diversion issue addressed partially).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment creates Reserve Fund; effective Oct 1, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satellite Offices Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA requires the USPTO to establish three or more satellite offices in the U.S., subject to available resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offices to be established within three years after Sept 16, 2011 (by Sept 16, 2014). USPTO Director must report to Congress every three years on rationale, progress, and whether offices achieve purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA authorizes USPTO to prioritize examination at the request of an applicant for products/processes/technologies important to U.S. economy or competitiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amends §2(b)(2); effective Sept 16, 2012.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Claims Directed to or Encompassing a Human Organism (Weldon Amendment codification)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA permanently prohibits issuance of patents on claims directed to or encompassing a human organism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies prohibition notwithstanding any other law. Effective on applications pending on or filed after Sept 16, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of 60-Day Period for Patent Term Adjustments (§156(d)(1) timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA amends how the 60-day period for regulatory approvals (e.g., FDA) is calculated: transmissions after 4:30 p.m. ET on a business day are deemed received the next business day; other timing clarifications consistent with prior case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to applications pending on, filed after, or decisions subject to judicial review as of Sept 16, 2011. References Medicines Co. v. Kappos decision for timing practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on Misconduct Before the Office (biennial)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA requires USPTO Director to report to House and Senate Judiciary Committees every two years on the impact of the new statute-of-limitations provision regarding misconduct before the Office, including instances where proceedings were barred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report required beginning after Sept 16, 2011; chart lists as Report on Misconduct Before the Office (Sec. 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Business Study (impact of eliminating first-to-invent)
rubrics_metrics.description: AIA requires SBA and USPTO to study within one year how eliminating first-to-invent affects small businesses' ability to obtain patents and report to Senate and House Small Business and Judiciary Committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study due within 1 year of Sept 16, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on Prior User Rights (comparative study)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires USPTO Director to report to Judiciary Committees within four months of Sept 16, 2011 on the operation of prior user rights in other industrialized countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report due Jan 16, 2012 per Table of Effective Dates entry (four months after Sept 16, 2011).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report on Satellite Offices (triennial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires USPTO Director to report to Congress every three years on rationale for satellite office locations, progress establishing offices, and whether offices are achieving purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also requires a study within 4 years on AIA implementation effects on innovation, competitiveness and small business access to capital. Initial satellite office establishment due by Sept 16, 2014; first triennial report thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study of the America Invents Act (implementation study)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires USPTO Director to conduct a study not later than nine months after Sept 16, 2011 on effective ways of promoting [implementation and effects].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study scheduled and referenced; Table of Effective Dates indicates study due Sept 16, 2015 (Study of AIA due date entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study on Genetic Testing (confirmatory testing study)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires study into independent confirming genetic diagnostic test activity where gene patents and exclusive licensing for primary genetic diagnostic tests exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study due June 16, 2012 per Table of Effective Dates entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing Methods for Studying Diversity of Applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires USPTO Director to establish methods for studying diversity of patent applicants (including minorities, women, veterans) and report to Congress within six months of Sept 16, 2011.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods must be established and a report provided; effective/milestone timing reflected in table (March 16, 2012 listed in Table of Effective Dates as three months? chart lists timing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study on International Patent Protections for Small Businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires USPTO Director, in consultation with Commerce Secretary and SBA, to study and report on helping small businesses with international patent protection, including a potential revolving fund loan/grant program to defray costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report due to Congress within 120 days from Sept 16, 2011 (Jan 14, 2012).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study of Patent Litigation (by GAO re: NPEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires Government Accountability Office to study the impact of patent infringement litigation by non-practicing entities/patent assertion entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study to be completed by Sept 16, 2012.
